description: Conformance vectors for H61A0 over ble. Every SDK — the Rust core, its bindings and any hand-written port — must produce exactly these bytes for these arguments. The wire carries no envelope here, so a vector states `frames_hex` and no `message`. See ../README.md.

vectors.name: power on
vectors.source: docs/protocol/ble.md 2.1 — exercised on the unit

vectors.name: power off
vectors.source: docs/protocol/ble.md 2.1 — exercised on the unit

vectors.name: brightness 50%
vectors.source: docs/protocol/ble.md 2.2 — exercised on the unit

vectors.name: colour red over every zone the mask reaches
vectors.source: docs/protocol/ble.md 2.3 — exercised on the unit; the mask ends 7f, not ff, because bit 15 reaches nothing

vectors.name: colour green over zones 0 and 2 only
vectors.source: docs/protocol/ble.md 2.3 — exercised on the unit; least significant bit first, so zones 0 and 2 are 0x05

vectors.name: 4000 K with the rendering the caller supplies
vectors.source: docs/protocol/ble.md 2.3 — exercised on the unit; the white triplet is whatever the caller passes, the codec renders nothing

vectors.name: brightness of zones 0 and 1
vectors.source: docs/protocol/ble.md 2.4 — exercised on the unit

vectors.name: all fifteen zone brightnesses at once
vectors.source: docs/protocol/ble.md 2.5 — exercised on the unit

vectors.name: zone interpolation on
vectors.source: docs/protocol/ble.md 2.6 — exercised on the unit

vectors.name: zone interpolation off
vectors.source: docs/protocol/ble.md 2.6 — exercised on the unit

vectors.name: status: power, then brightness
vectors.source: docs/protocol/ble.md 3 — both reads exercised on the unit, which answered aa 01 and aa 04 in turn

vectors.name: read the segment count
vectors.source: docs/protocol/ble.md 3 — exercised on the unit, which answered 15

vectors.name: read the IC count
vectors.source: docs/protocol/ble.md 3 — exercised on the unit, which answered 00 2a

vectors.name: read the Wi-Fi MAC
vectors.source: docs/protocol/ble.md 3 — exercised on the unit

vectors.name: read the hardware version
vectors.source: docs/protocol/ble.md 3 — exercised on the unit, which answered 1.02.00

vectors.name: read the software version
vectors.source: docs/protocol/ble.md 3 — exercised on the unit, which answered 2.06.02

vectors.name: read the dynamic API type
vectors.source: docs/protocol/ble.md 3 — exercised on the unit, which answered 2

vectors.name: read the first zone group
vectors.source: docs/protocol/ble.md 3 — the request was exercised on the unit; the layout of the answer was not established, so the file declares no reply

vectors.name: read the last zone group
vectors.source: docs/protocol/ble.md 3 — exercised on the unit

vectors.name: Wi-Fi provisioning, SSID Test, password abc, UTC+2
vectors.source: docs/protocol/ble.md 4 — worked out from the documented layout, NOT captured and never sent to a device; this pins the encoder, not the firmware

vectors.name: Wi-Fi provisioning with an empty password
vectors.source: docs/protocol/ble.md 4 — worked out from the documented layout, never sent to a device; an empty password is the single byte 0x00

vectors.name: Wi-Fi provisioning carrying the API block, three data frames
vectors.source: docs/protocol/ble.md 4 — worked out from the documented layout, never sent to a device; the URL is what a device answering API type 2 is told to use

errors.name: brightness 0 is rejected, never clamped to 1
brightness above 100 is rejected, never clamped
colour temperature below the device range
a zone the mask cannot carry is rejected, not dropped in silence
more zone brightnesses than there are zones
a timezone offset in minutes that is not minutes
an SSID longer than the field can carry
an argument the command does not declare
a command this mode does not carry
the API block is a command of its own, not an argument to add
